what: comfy_kitchen.int8_attention (ComfyUI's --use-ck-attention path; stock kernel design, unchanged on the fork) on the block-49 and block-0 captures, plain and with the ChannelBalance weights fold applied to the inputs
conditions: 2026-09-15, served wheel 0.2.34+sol.5284cfb (int8_attention is untouched by the fork's commits), first 8 heads, S=104361, referent fp32 dense attention on the same bf16 inputs (bench/analyze_sol_error.py::dense_reference), rel L2 with the plain dense norm as denominator
reading: block 49 is about 8x block 0 on this kernel too, so the last block's attention shape makes any rounding expensive here as well; but the weights fold removes about 1%, against 13% on Sol and 7% on sage, and the plain error is 0.0166 against Sol's 0.0265 and sage fp8++'s 0.0487 on the same heads. The loud-channel mechanism does not apply to this kernel: it rotates Q and K before quantizing, so no channel can dominate a shared scale. The rebalance is not a fix for it, and it is the most accurate INT8 attention on this block that this repo has measured.
source_note: comfy_kitchen/sage_attention.py::int8_attention docstring: 'Q and K receive the same fused block-Hadamard rotation before INT8'; backends/cuda/sage_attention/quant_qk_int8.cu: a fixed random diagonal then a normalized Walsh-Hadamard (H64 or H128) inside the quantizer, one absmax scale per token block per head AFTER the rotation, and K centred on a detected anchor key (detect_k_anchor). The rotation is orthogonal, so q.k is unchanged; it spreads any per-channel or per-token outlier across all 128 channels, which is the structural version of what the rebalance does per channel. Always on; no option.
not_established: speed of this kernel against sage fp8++ and Sol at H3 length on this card (not timed here); whether its P and V INT8 error is what remains at block 49 (its ratio to block 0 says the amplifier is at work on something)
